name: Philip
title: One of the Twelve
tagline: From Bethsaida; the one who told Nathanael, “Come and see.”
story: One of the Twelve, from Bethsaida; Jesus found him and called him, and Philip brought Nathanael to meet Jesus.

entries.title: Of Bethsaida
entries.text: “Philip was of Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter” (John 1:44); John calls it “Bethsaida of Galilee” (John 12:21).

entries.title: No family named
entries.text: Scripture names no family for Philip the apostle.

entries.title: Married, says Clement
entries.text: Clement of Alexandria (about 200), quoted by Eusebius, counts Philip among the apostles who married: “Peter and Philip begat children; and Philip also gave his daughters in marriage.” Polycrates (about 190) speaks of Philip’s “two aged virgin daughters” at Hierapolis and “another daughter” who rests at Ephesus.

verses.text: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these; The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;
Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the publican; James the son of Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus;
Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.
And Simon he surnamed Peter;
And James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and he surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder:
And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Canaanite,
And Judas Iscariot, which also betrayed him: and they went into an house.
Simon, (whom he also named Peter,) and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,
Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphæus, and Simon called Zelotes,
And Judas the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitor.

And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James.

verses.text: And he goeth up into a mountain, and calleth unto him whom he would: and they came unto him.
And he ordained twelve, that they should be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach,
And to have power to heal sicknesses, and to cast out devils:
And Simon he surnamed Peter;
And James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and he surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder:
And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Canaanite,
And Judas Iscariot, which also betrayed him: and they went into an house.
And it came to pass in those days, that he went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God.
¶ And when it was day, he called unto him his disciples: and of them he chose twelve, whom also he named apostles;
Simon, (whom he also named Peter,) and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,
Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphæus, and Simon called Zelotes,
And Judas the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitor.

places.name: Hierapolis
places.note: Polycrates (about 190) says “Philip, one of the twelve apostles” sleeps here; the city is named in Scripture only at Colossians 4:13

quote.text: The day following Jesus would go forth into Galilee, and findeth Philip, and saith unto him, Follow me. Now Philip was of Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter.

claim.text: In John 1 he is the only one Jesus himself finds and calls with “Follow me” (John 1:43); Andrew and the other disciple follow at the Baptist’s word, Peter is brought by Andrew, and Nathanael by Philip. Matthew, Mark and Luke name Philip only in the lists of the Twelve.
From the same town (John 1:44). With Andrew he brings the Greeks’ request to Jesus (John 12:22), and both speak up before the feeding of the five thousand (John 6:7–8).
“Philip findeth Nathanael, and saith unto him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write” (John 1:45).
In the lists of Matthew, Mark and Luke Bartholomew is named straight after Philip (Matt 10:3; Mark 3:18; Luke 6:14).

family.text: Scripture names no family for Philip the apostle.

Clement of Alexandria (about 200), quoted by Eusebius, counts Philip among the apostles who married: “Peter and Philip begat children; and Philip also gave his daughters in marriage.” Polycrates (about 190) speaks of Philip’s “two aged virgin daughters” at Hierapolis and “another daughter” who rests at Ephesus.

identifications.text: Three other men called Philip appear in the New Testament: Philip the evangelist, one of the Seven (Acts 6:5; 21:8), Philip the tetrarch (Luke 3:1), and Herodias’s husband Philip (Mark 6:17). This page is about the apostle.

The Philip who preached in Samaria and baptized the Ethiopian (Acts 8:5–40) is taken to be the evangelist, not the apostle: the believers were scattered “except the apostles” (Acts 8:1), “the apostles which were at Jerusalem” sent Peter and John to his converts (Acts 8:14), and Acts leaves him at Caesarea (Acts 8:40), where Philip the evangelist lives in Acts 21:8.

scripture.text: Scripture says nothing of Philip the apostle after the upper room (Acts 1:13).

tradition.text: Papias, “their contemporary”, heard “a wonderful tale from the daughters of Philip”; Eusebius says “Philip the apostle dwelt at Hierapolis with his daughters”.

argument.text: Proclus speaks of “four prophetesses, the daughters of Philip” at Hierapolis. Acts gives Philip the evangelist “four daughters, virgins, which did prophesy” (Acts 21:8–9). Eusebius sets the two reports side by side without comment.

verses.43012021: The same came therefore to Philip, which was of Bethsaida of Galilee, and desired him, saying, Sir, we would see Jesus.

verses.43014008: Philip saith unto him, Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth us.
verses.43014009: Jesus saith unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father; and how sayest thou then, Shew us the Father?
